roadmap_gap.anchor: Phase 12 complex production drivers and heavy helper consumers

required_features.evidence: The bounded starter still does not claim DMA mapping, scatter-gather command assembly, virtqueue buffer ownership, or live request or response buffer lifetime.

The landed queue-family planner, host-limit summary, queue-depth summary, and io-queue-map summaries keep control, event, request, and poll topology reviewable in memory without claiming live blk-mq submission or request completion.

The lane records freeze or restore planning, queue-depth restore pressure, queue-map restore pressure, event-buffer refill pressure, and restore sequencing, but it does not claim measured throughput, command completion, event-work recycling, or PM callback parity.
The current packet stays intentionally segmented across the bounded driver starter, direct tests, survey note, and archival raw-GitHub fallback catalog instead of presenting a full runtime SCSI port.

gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 12 build gate now carries both the existing virtio_scsi survey and the queue-layout, host-limit, plus io-queue-map tests so this complex-driver lane stays reviewable without widening into runtime transport code.
The existing make target keeps the survey lane and the bounded driver test lane runnable in the same way as the other tranche checkpoints instead of hiding them behind ad hoc commands.

The Phase 10 virtio core slice already covers status sequencing, feature negotiation, queue callback bookkeeping, descriptor-shape metadata, and notification accounting, which is the minimum shared footing a future virtio_scsi starter depends on.

The existing virtio_ring helper keeps queue-shape and notification bookkeeping in memory only, which is the closest current Zigux surface for describing virtio_scsi control, event, request, and poll-queue topology without claiming DMA-backed queue execution.
A dedicated survey test still matters after the starter landed because it records the remaining roadmap gap around SCSI host lifecycle, TMF handling, event work, and DMA-backed request flow.

The lane needs a note that compares the landed queue planner, recovery helper, probe snapshot, host-limit summary, queue-depth summary, and io-queue-map summaries against the much larger virtio_scsi.c surface so future runs do not mistake this bounded foothold for a production SCSI HBA port.

The first honest virtio_scsi starter is now landed around an in-memory queue-family planner that models control, event, request, and request_poll virtqueue topology, preserves the Linux rule that poll queues must still leave one default request queue, and records a lab-only freeze or restore summary that blocks planning while transport is frozen and clears queue state after restore.

Dedicated driver tests now keep the starter honest around poll-queue clamping, stable global virtqueue indexes, the bounded freeze or restore contract, repeated transport-reset replanning across recovery generations, fresh recovery queue-depth and io-queue-map summaries after restore, the host-limit summary helper that clamps cmd_per_lun, and the queue-depth summary helper that mirrors `virtscsi_change_queue_depth()` before any Scsi_Host registration work.

Dedicated syntax-lab coverage now keeps the bounded export surface for the queue lab, request-queue enums, descriptor flags, probe snapshot, host-limit summary, queue-depth summary, io-queue-map summary, and recovery summaries reviewable without claiming live DMA or `Scsi_Host` lifecycle work.

Dedicated recovery-state coverage now proves restore clears stale queue-depth state, replans later freeze generations, keeps the bounded recovery-event-refill summary aligned with the replanned frozen topology, and keeps the bounded transport-reset packet honest before any live `scsi_scan_host()`, blk-mq submission, or DMA-backed request flow is attempted.

The slice note records exactly what the queue-layout, probe snapshot, host-limit summary, queue-depth summary, and io-queue-map starters cover so the survey can stay focused on the deeper transport, SCSI-host, and DMA-backed work that is still intentionally missing.

The lane now needs one exact read-only fallback packet that pins the current inspected head, the three public tree entry points, and the ten commit-pinned raw GitHub artifact URLs with recorded byte counts and sha256 hashes so future scheduled runs can recover the real survey surface when connector-backed reads are flaky.

The landed probe snapshot helper now records virtscsi_probe() config fields such as num_queues, seg_max, cmd_per_lun, max_target, max_lun, and max_sectors, plus the derived control or event versus request virtqueue layout before any blk-mq submission, TMF, or DMA-backed queue work is attempted.

The landed host-limit summary helper now takes the probe snapshot one step farther by clamping cmd_per_lun against a synthetic `can_queue` and recording the derived `max_target`, `max_lun`, `max_sectors`, and `nr_hw_queues` values before any `scsi_host_alloc()`, `scsi_add_host()`, `scsi_scan_host()`, blk-mq mapping, or DMA-backed request flow is attempted.

The landed queue-depth summary helper now reuses the bounded host-limit summary to mirror `virtscsi_change_queue_depth()`, clamping a requested depth against effective `cmd_per_lun` while keeping `track_queue_depth` reviewable before any live `Scsi_Host` registration, blk-mq submission, or DMA-backed request flow is attempted.

The landed io-queue-map summary helpers now keep the bounded default, read, and poll map counts, queue offsets, virtio-affinity intent, and poll-map restore pressure reviewable before any live `map_queues` callback, CPU-affinity wiring, blk-mq submission, or DMA-backed request flow is attempted.

Command submission, TMF and async notification handling, event-work scheduling, virtqueue buffer ownership, scsi_add_host(), scsi_scan_host(), live blk-mq queue mapping callbacks, PM freeze or restore wiring, and DMA-backed request flow remain blocked even though the smaller probe snapshot, host-limit summary, queue-depth summary, and io-queue-map helpers are now landed.
